Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed, homogeneous mass in the right upper lung zone. Pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma (PPSS) typically presents as a sharply defined, non-invasive mass on imaging, often without significant adjacent vessel invasion or pleural effusion, distinguishing it from more aggressive malignancies like primary lung cancer.
